report.summary: Observed directly: from 2026-11-21T16:20:55Z the PostgreSQL instance in namespace astronomy-shop (pod postgresql-6bd9b846cb-pzrsb) rejects every connection of role "otelu" with 'FATAL: password authentication failed' (pg_hba scram-sha-256), and from that minute the two postgres-backed services fail in their own spans/logs: product-catalog (ListProducts: 'failed to query products: pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"'; GetProduct: 'Product Not Found: <id>' for at least six different product IDs) and product-reviews (psycopg2.OperationalError same auth failure). That breaks checkout, product and product-review pages in frontend and frontend-proxy (HTTP 500 spans, '13 INTERNAL: failed to prepare order: failed to get product #"OLJCESPC7Z"'), and the load-generator reports fail_ratio 0.7333; error-line counts were still rising in the 3 minutes ending 16:21:16 (frontend 5→40, postgresql FATAL 5→27, product-reviews 8→20, recommendation 8→16). Database initialisation itself succeeded at 16:19:46 (CREATE ROLE/CREATE DATABASE, INSERT 0 10 products, INSERT 0 50 reviews) and the same product-reviews pod served GetProductReviews with gRPC status 0 and HTTP 200 at 16:20:46.9–16:20:49.3, then failed at 16:20:55.7. So the credential state of the postgres role changed (or was invalidated) between 16:20:49 and 16:20:55 while the DB stayed up, which points at the postgresql workload as the origin of the fault; who or what altered the credential, and the credential values themselves, are not observable (redacted Secret/inline values, change_history not integrated), so this is a partial conclusion. Product-catalog's Deployment was also switched at 16:20:49 to read DB_CONNECTION_STRING from a Secret, but that change alone cannot explain product-reviews failing on an unchanged pod, so it is recorded as a rejected single-cause hypothesis rather than the root cause.

Its variant is off in flagd-config, and the failures cover at least six different product IDs plus an explicit 'pq: password authentication failed for user "otelu"' error on ListProducts, which a per-product flag would not produce.

Rejected: pod-level resource exhaustion, crash or eviction on the failing services. No actor or record of the credential change was observed: no Kubernetes event names the postgresql workload or a credential object, no ConfigMap/Secret change is visible, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
The relationship between the two 'terminating connection due to administrator command' backends at 16:20:57Z and the credential change is unknown; no session/statement log is available.

Telemetry only covers the rebuilt environment: Jaeger holds traces from ~16:20:37Z, Loki lines from ~16:19:42Z, and kubernetes objects are the state at query time; nothing before 16:19:38Z is observable, so no earlier incident in the 24h window can be assessed.

Trace metrics gave no samples in the window: traces_span_metrics_calls_total has series metadata (service_name values including product-catalog, product-reviews, frontend; status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR/STATUS_CODE_UNSET) but instant and range queries returned no data, so error rates and latency distributions could not be quantified from metrics.

Impact on accounting was not verified: its pod started at 16:20:53–16:20:56Z and its read logs stop at 'Connecting to Kafka: kafka:9092' with no database error observed, so its PostgreSQL path is unchecked.

Search PostgreSQL and audit logs for an ALTER ROLE / DROP ROLE / password-rotation action on role otelu around 16:20:50–16:20:57Z, including any superuser (root) session, to identify what applied the change.

service:
  extensions: [jaeger_storage, jaeger_query, healthcheckv2]
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [jaeger_storage_exporter]
  telemetry:
    resource:
      service.name: jaeger
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
        - periodic:
            interval: 10000
            timeout: 5000
            exporter:
              otlp:
                protocol: http/protobuf
                endpoint: http://${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_HOST}:${env:OTEL_COLLECTOR_PORT_HTTP}
                insecure: true
    logs:
      level: info
extensions:
  healthcheckv2:
    use_v2: true
    http:
      endpoint: 0.0.0.0:13133
  jaeger_query:
    storage:
      traces: memory_backend
      metrics: metrics_backend
    base_path: /jaeger/ui
  jaeger_storage:
    backends:
      memory_backend:
        memory:
          max_traces: ${env:MEMORY_MAX_TRACES}
    metric_backends:
      metrics_backend:
        prometheus:
          endpoint: "http://${env:PROMETHEUS_ADDR}"
          normalize_calls: true
          normalize_duration: true

receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:JAEGER_HOST}:${env:JAEGER_GRPC_PORT}

processors:
  batch:

exporters:
  jaeger_storage_exporter:
    trace_storage: memory_backend
